newsitem.title: UK: Joking aside,German workers lead the way in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Joking aside,German workers lead the way in Europe.

text.p: Germany's workforce is the envy of Europe -- more efficient, better educated, harder working and enjoying better working conditions than other Europeans, according to a survey published by British investment capital group 3i on Monday.
But German workers apparently just can't take a joke.
"They are universally perceived as lacking in humour, an opinion shared even by their own managers," the survey of 490 managers in small and medium-sized firms across Europe showed.
Spain and Italy came off worst in the survey. Spanish workers were branded less punctual, less trustworthy, less efficient and more reluctant to work hard.

The report found that the greatest disparity between the workforces of Germany, France, Britain, Italy and Spain lay in educational standards. Germany came top of the educational league table while Spain registered the worst score of the countries surveyed.
Spain chalked up another negative score of minus 23 for punctuality, while the Germans excelled with a score of 66.
Britain obtained the lowest score for the power of its unions, which lost many of their rights during 18 years of Conservative government, and for job security.
But the report revealed that while each of the countries surveyed ranked the German workforce highest, nationalism crept into each country's view of their own workforce.
"Managers in each of the countries surveyed were generally willing to admit to some weakness in their own workforce," said 3i marketing director Adam Quarry.
"It is, however, of concern to see such low appreciation of workers, employment and government in the Mediterranean countries of Italy and Spain by their counterparts further north in Europe."
